resources.string: To open Notification Inbox, swipe down on empty home-screen space, then slide back up toward where you started without lifting your finger. Release to open.
App guide
Navigation
Notification Inbox
Common tasks
Open your inbox

Enable notification access for Comfer in Android settings. Tap anywhere in the home notification row to open All apps. You can also swipe down on empty home-screen space, slide back up toward where you started without lifting, and release to open the inbox. App icons show which apps have notifications; they are not separate buttons. When nothing is visible, an inbox icon keeps the entry available.
The three bottom tabs

All apps (inbox icon): returns to current, visible notifications across apps and exits selection or configuration.

Saved (archive): shows locally saved notifications with a search input, only after they leave the active notification list. A notification never appears in both lists. Uses the same grouped or chronological view as Active. Tap a long preview to expand it, then tap again to open its app (the original notification destination is not retained). Long press to select, tap more copies or a group title to select them, and use Delete at the bottom. For one selected copy, More actions offers the same app protection and Android notification settings controls as Active. App protection also removes that app’s saved copies and stops its History capture. Create content rule opens a draft using its app/profile and saved title or message. Edit the suggested phrase and preview it against the saved reference; rules start in test-only mode. Multiple deletion requires confirmation. Back or Cancel exits selection. Swipe a copy to delete only that local copy. Copies whose preview is empty or hidden by Android are not saved. Enable capture under Settings → History.

Settings (gear): opens a directory for Quiet hours, Filters, History and Connection and privacy. Quiet hours contains separate Focus timers and Recurring schedule pages. Android Back returns to the parent page. The gear returns to the settings directory from a child page.
Read, select and navigate

Notification bodies initially show one line. If more text is available, the first tap expands the full body and the next tap opens its destination in the source app. A single-line notification opens on the first tap. After a successful open, Comfer requests dismissal of eligible notifications. With History enabled, an eligible copy is saved first and becomes available in Saved after the notification leaves Active. Failed opens leave the notification active. Long press to enter selection mode and select that notification. Small rings become visible in their reserved space in front of every card; selected rings become solid circles. Text stays aligned when selection starts or ends. In selection mode, tap cards or rings to select or deselect them.

Swipe a notification left or right to dismiss it when allowed; the card slides fully off-screen before removal. Protected or ongoing notifications cannot be dismissed through Comfer.

App groups show the app name and an up or down caret. Tap the caret to collapse or expand its notifications. In selection mode, tap the app name to select every notification in that group, including collapsed ones; tap it again when all are selected to deselect the group. Other groups keep their selections. Chronological view shows a flat list with newest items first. Scroll upward to use the full screen. Use Android Back to close More actions, leave selection or return from Settings. Returning from Android notification settings brings the selected notification back into view.
Actions on a notification

Long press a notification for the bottom quick menu.

Snooze: asks Android to bring selected notifications back in 15 minutes. Shown on Android 8 or newer only when every selected item is eligible.

Priority: places the selected apps first in grouped view. If all are already prioritized, it removes their priority; otherwise it prioritizes all of them. Android alert priority does not change.

More actions: available for a single selected notification and opens app controls. With multiple selections, only shared actions are shown. Cancel appears for multiple selections and clears them. Deselecting the last item exits selection automatically; Android Back also exits selection.
Dismiss, snooze and batch selection

Swipe a notification left or right to ask Android to dismiss it immediately. This removes the source notification; there is no swipe confirmation. Protected and ongoing notifications remain.

To dismiss several items, long press one and tap other cards or rings. Dismiss selected appears only when every selected notification is eligible. Tap it, then Confirm dismiss selected. If an item changes or disappears before execution, it may be skipped; a message appears if an action could not be completed.

Snooze in the quick menu postpones eligible selected notifications for 15 minutes. Snooze requires Android 8 or newer. Use Cancel or Android Back to leave selection without performing an action.
More actions: app controls

Protect this app from dismissal blocks Comfer’s dismissal and snooze actions for the app. Remove app protection restores eligible actions. Android may still protect ongoing notifications.\n\nSound and notification settings opens Android’s controls for the notification category or app. Use those controls to change sounds or disable alerts. For another profile, open the app’s settings inside that profile.
Inbox configuration

Notification view offers Grouped by app and Chronological side by side. The highlighted choice is active. Grouped by app puts priority apps first; Chronological shows the newest notifications first.

Below the view choices in Notification settings, Pause rules, schedules and timers / Resume rules, schedules and timers controls Comfer’s scheduled behavior and device quiet requests. Filters also supports content rules: choose app/channel, title/message fields, required and exception phrases, preview, and save. Rules start in test-only mode. Disable Test only to act; auto-dismiss requires separate confirmation and affects future events only. Regex is deferred.

Last successful refresh shows when the inbox last synced. Refresh connection retries synchronization. Device DND settings opens Android’s Do Not Disturb controls.

Reset notification settings requires confirmation, clears Comfer’s notification preferences and leaves automation paused. It does not dismiss your source notifications.
Focus timers and recurring quiet hours

Device quiet uses Android Do Not Disturb and requires separate DND access. The access button appears only while permission is missing. Android priority exceptions still apply.

Focus 15, 30 or 60 min starts a temporary quiet period. The timer shows its end time. End focus timer appears while a timer is set and ends Comfer’s timer; an active schedule or other Android rules can still keep the device quiet. Restarting the phone ends a manual timer.

On Android 12 or newer, use Allow precise timing in Focus timers or a device-quiet recurring schedule to grant Alarms & reminders access. Without it, Android may delay timer endings and schedule changes.

For a recurring schedule, tap Start and End to choose exact times, select weekdays and grant DND access if needed. Tap Save and enable schedule to save changes. Disable schedule stops the recurring schedule. Schedules can cross midnight and use the displayed device time zone.

Android may delay schedule changes while idle. Check the shown Comfer status, Android Do Not Disturb status and next boundary when troubleshooting.
Live notifications and unavailable previews

The main inbox displays current notifications in memory. With History enabled, opening an eligible notification saves its copy first. After opening succeeds, Comfer requests dismissal when allowed. A saved copy appears in History after the live notification is removed. Optional History saves encrypted local text copies of future eligible notifications after consent. Copies remain until retention expiry or deletion and cannot use the original notification action. Choose 24 hours, 7 days or 30 days and exclude apps in History. Search finds copies by text, app and date. History is limited to 500 copies and is excluded from configuration backups. Locked, secret and protected events are skipped; capture can have gaps. Android may hide sensitive text or provide a limited preview; use Open for the full content. Calls, alarms, media and other protected ongoing notifications may have fewer available actions.
How to open and keep a notification

Enable History under Settings → History to retain eligible copies. Tap a notification to expand a long preview, then tap again to open its destination. A one-line preview opens immediately. After launch, Comfer requests dismissal. Find the saved copy in Saved after it leaves Active. Android-redacted, secret and protected content is not saved. If History is off, opened notifications are dismissed without creating a copy.
How to silence one app

1. Long press one of the app’s notifications.
2. Tap More actions, then Sound and notification settings.
3. In Android settings, silence the category or change the app’s allowed notifications. Available controls vary by phone and app.

Use Android Back to return to the selected notification.
How to focus now or quiet notifications overnight

For a short break: open Settings → Quiet hours → Focus timers, grant DND access if prompted, then choose Focus 15, 30 or 60 min. Resume schedules and timers first if it is paused.\n\nFor nights: open Quiet hours → Recurring schedule and set a start time such as 22:00 and an end time such as 07:00, choose the start weekdays, then tap Save and enable schedule. Review Android priority exceptions for the alerts you still want.
How to clear several notifications

1. Long press a notification to select it.
2. Tap other cards or their rings; solid circles mark selected items.
3. If all selected items support dismissal, tap Dismiss selected, then Confirm dismiss selected.

For one notification, swipe it left or right to dismiss directly. For multiple selections, Cancel clears the selection. Deselect the last item or use Android Back to exit selection. Protected items cannot be dismissed through Comfer.
How to find missing notifications

First check Saved and the sorting choice in Settings. If access is missing, tap Notification access and enable Comfer. If the inbox is reconnecting, use Refresh connection. If it still cannot reconnect, turn Comfer notification access off and on in Android settings.\n\nA healthy empty inbox means there are no current notifications in that view. If History was enabled when a notification arrived, its saved copy may still be available in the Saved tab. Enabling History cannot recover earlier dismissed notifications.
